title: How Does a 400-Ton Plane Fly? ✈️
description: A wing doesn't fly by magic — it pushes air down, and the air pushes the wing up! Plus the famous myth that's still taught wrong in schools.

scenes.say: A giant airliner can weigh more than four hundred tons, yet it rises into the sky like a feather. So what's the secret?

scenes.caption: The angled wing
scenes.say: It's all in the wing. Its curved shape and slight tilt push huge amounts of air downward.
Newton's third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Air pushed down pushes the wing up. That's lift.

right.label: Myth
right.sub: Air on top catches up with air below

left.label: Truth
left.sub: Air on top is much faster and never meets

scenes.say: There's a famous myth that air over the wing speeds up to meet the air below. In reality, it moves much faster and the two never meet.

scenes.label: Typical cruising speed
scenes.say: The faster you go, the more lift you get. That's why airliners cruise at around nine hundred kilometers per hour.
